The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Looking at this problem, I need to understand what happens when Mark repeatedly replaces pairs $(a,b)$ with $(\gcd(a,b), \text{lcm}(a,b))$.

**Key Invariant:** Since $\gcd(a,b) \cdot \text{lcm}(a,b) = ab$ and $\nu_p(\gcd(a,b)) + \nu_p(\text{lcm}(a,b)) = \nu_p(a) + \nu_p(b)$, the multiset of $p$-adic valuations for each prime $p$ is preserved throughout.

**Terminal Condition:** Mark stops when no move changes the numbers, meaning for every pair on the board, one divides the other. The numbers must form a **divisibility chain**: $n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$.

**Uniqueness of the Final State:** In a divisibility chain, for each prime $p$, the sequence $\nu_p(n_1) \leq \nu_p(n_2) \leq \cdots \leq \nu_p(n_{2100})$ must be non-decreasing. Since the multiset of exponents is fixed, the $i$-th number has, for each prime $p$, the $i$-th **smallest** exponent from $\{1, 2, \ldots, 2100\}$.

**Finding the 2026th smallest number:** The $i$-th smallest exponent of prime $p$ is the smallest $k$ such that the number of integers in $\{1,\ldots,2100\}$ with $\nu_p(n) \leq k$ is at least $i$. This equals $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p^{k+1} \rfloor \geq i$.

For $i = 2026$: I need $\lfloor 2100/p^{k+1} \rfloor \leq 2100 - 2026 = 74$.

| Prime $p$ | $\lfloor 2100/p\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^2\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^3\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^4\rfloor$ | Exponent $k$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 2 | 1050 | 525 | 262 | **65** | **4** |
| 3 | 700 | 233 | 77 | **25** | **3** |
| 5 | 420 | 84 | **16** | — | **2** |
| 7 | 300 | **42** | — | — | **1** |
| 11 | 190 | **17** | — | — | **1** |
| 13 | 161 | **12** | — | — | **1** |
| 17 | 123 | **7** | — | — | **1** |
| 19 | 110 | **5** | — | — | **1** |
| 23 | 91 | **3** | — | — | **1** |
| 29 | **72** | — | — | — | **0** |

For all primes $p \geq 29$: $\lfloor 2100/p \rfloor \leq 72 \leq 74$, so the exponent is 0.

**The 2026th smallest number is:**
$$2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^1 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

**Number of divisors:**
$$\tau = (4+1)(3+1)(1+1)^7 = 5 \times 4 \times 2^7 = 20 \times 128 = 2560$$

$$\boxed{2560}$$
